headline: ModelBest, developer of the MiniCPM family of models, has open-sourced MiniCPM-V 4.7, an image-and-text AI model it says runs on an iPhone using about 3GB of memory.
score_reason: Pool score 5 kept: a notable on-device open release, but the speed and test figures are the company's own and come from one outlet.
importance_line: People who want an image-reading AI that works privately and offline on a phone or laptop get another open option, and QbitAI's hands-on tests reportedly handled charts and papers offline, but the speed, memory and test figures are ModelBest's own and rest on one outlet's account.
summary: Pandaily reports that ModelBest has open-sourced MiniCPM-V 4.7 in 35-billion-parameter and 1-billion-parameter sizes, the larger being the first mixture-of-experts model (a design that activates only part of the model for each piece of text) in the MiniCPM-V series, with code and weights released under the Apache-2.0 licence. ModelBest says the larger version, which uses about 3 billion parameters at a time, runs on an iPhone 17 Pro Max in about 3GB of memory at more than 13 tokens (small chunks of text) per second, using a technique it calls lookahead expert scheduling; its speed and test scores, such as 91.72 on MMBench, are the company's own.
notes: The visible page was blank in curl; the article text was read from the page's embedded data. Company claims, one outlet.
